blocks.text: Pituitary gland is attached to hypothalamus by a stalk called infundibulum. Pituitary gland is divided into three lobes called the anterior pituitary, posterior pituitary and intermediate / median pituitary.
Anterior pituitary secretes many hormones, many of which regulate the activity of other endocrine glands.

items: Growth Hormone (GH, or somatotropin) stimulates the growth of muscles, bones (indirectly), and other tissues. It is also essential for proper metabolic regulation.
Adrenocorticotropic Hormone (ACTH, or corticotropin) stimulates the adrenal cortex for the secretion of corticosteroids (cortisone and aldosterone), which regulate glucose and salt homeostasis.
Thyroid-stimulating Hormone (TSH, or thyrotropin) stimulates the thyroid gland to produce thyroxine, which in turn stimulates oxidative respiration.
Luteinizing Hormone (LH) In females, it stimulates ovaries to produce progesterone and estrogen hormones. It also initiates ovulation. In males, it stimulates testes for testosterone production.
Follicle-stimulating Hormone (FSH) stimulates the development of ovarian follicles in females. In males, it stimulated the development of sperms. FSH and LH are both referred to as gonadotropins.
Prolactin stimulates the mammary glands to produce milk. It is produced in both male and female but functions only in female.

blocks.title: Tidbit
blocks.text:
Growth Hormone Treatment
GH treatment is given to children have short stature due to GH deficiency. It improves their growth rate.
However, every dwarf person does not have GH deficiency. So, GH therapy may not be appropriate for everyone.
Some people use GH because they believe it will build muscle or slow aging. However, doctors do not support the use of GH for these purposes.

The posterior pituitary contains axons that originate in hypothalamus and extend to posterior pituitary. It does not synthesize any hormone but only stores and releases the hormones made by hypothalamus. The following are the hormones released by posterior pituitary.

items: Antidiuretic Hormone (ADH or vasopressin) stimulates water retention by the kidneys.
Oxytocin stimulates the milk-ejection by stimulating the contraction of smooth muscles of mammary glands. It also stimulates uterine contractions in women during childbirth.

blocks.title: For Information
blocks.text: During embryonic development, posterior pituitary is formed from an outgrowth of neural tissue. That’s why, hypothalamus of brain and posterior pituitary remain interconnected by a tract of axons.

blocks.alt: The hypothalamus with its stalk and the two pituitary lobes, with blood vessels to the anterior lobe and axons of the hypothalamus to the posterior lobe. Green arrows from the anterior pituitary: TSH to the thyroid, ACTH to the adrenal cortex, FSH and LH to the ovary and to the testis, GH to bones and skeletal muscles, prolactin to the mammary glands. Red arrows from the posterior pituitary: oxytocin to the mammary glands and the uterus, ADH to the kidney.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The printed Figure 16.3 draws the GH and prolactin arrows from beneath the posterior lobe; both are hormones of the anterior pituitary, so the drawing above takes them from the anterior lobe.

blocks.title: For Information
blocks.text: Oxytocin secretion continues after childbirth in breast-feeding mothers. That’s why, the uterus of a nursing mother returns to its normal size after pregnancy more quickly than the mothers who do not breast-feed.

In humans, intermediate pituitary is a thin layer of cells between the anterior and posterior pituitary. It produces melanocyte stimulating hormone (MSH). MSH stimulates the production and release of melanin by melanocytes in skin and hair.

items: If there is an over-secretion of growth hormone (GH) in a growing child, it causes gigantism i.e., height that is well above average, enlarged hands, feet, and facial features. Over-secretion of GH in adult life causes acromegaly in which bones are no longer capable of increasing in length but grow in thickness. Acromegaly is characterised by enlarged hands, feet, skull, nose and jawbone.
Deficiency of GH results in dwarfism in which development is much slower and individual has short stature. However, the body parts stay in proportion and brain development and IQ are unaffected.
Over secretion of TSH causes hyperthyroidism i.e., excess of thyroxine and its under secretion causes hypothyroidism i.e., lack of thyroxine.
Under secretion of ADH causes diabetes insipidus. It is characterized by excessive production of dilute urine and frequent thirst. Over secretion of ADH may lead to kidney problems.
Over secretion of oxytocin causes rupturing of uterine wall while under secretion of oxytocin inhibits normal labour process.
